segments.t: Left alone at Mathias's desk, Camille looks for the paternity document on his computer. Instead, she spots an open draft email detailing Mathias's ruthless plot to deceive author Ulrika. Let's listen to this chilling discovery in French first.
Voyons ce formulaire sur son ordinateur.
Attends, qu'est-ce que c'est que ça?
C'est un brouillon d'e-mail ouvert.
J'ai fait des promesses à Ulrika...
Pour qu'elle signe le contrat...
Mais je compte la décourager progressivement...
On peut la remplacer plus tard...
Utiliser la note de frais...
Pour une fondation animale...
Mon Dieu, c'est une trahison totale!
Il a menti à tout le monde.
Camille? Tu as trouvé ce formulaire?
Voici deux verres pour fêter ça!
Oui, tout va très bien, papa.
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Voyons ce formulaire sur son ordinateur.
'Let us look for this form on his computer.' Camille prepares to search for the legal paperwork. The imperative form 'voyons' expresses let us see.
Attends, qu'est-ce que c'est que ça?
'Wait, what is this?' Camille is distracted by an unexpected open window on the screen. The conversational phrase 'qu'est-ce que c'est' asks what something is.
C'est un brouillon d'e-mail ouvert.
'It is an open draft email.' Camille notices an unsent message written by Mathias. The compound noun 'brouillon d'e-mail' denotes a draft message.
J'ai fait des promesses à Ulrika...
'I made promises to Ulrika...' Camille reads the beginning of her father's private strategy notes. The noun 'promesses' denotes commitments or vows.
Pour qu'elle signe le contrat...
'So that she signs the contract...' Camille discovers how Mathias persuaded the Swedish author. The conjunction 'pour que' introduces a subjunctive purpose clause.
Mais je compte la décourager progressivement...
'But I plan to discourage her gradually...' Camille discovers his plan to push the author aside. The verb phrase 'compter faire' expresses an intention to act.
On peut la remplacer plus tard...
'We can replace her later on...' Camille reads that Mathias intends to bring in a new writer. The verb 'remplacer' means to substitute or replace.
Utiliser la note de frais...
'Use the expense account...' Camille uncovers his plan to charge the company for personal schemes. The business term 'note de frais' denotes an expense report.
Pour une fondation animale...
'For an animal foundation...' Camille reads how Mathias planned to feign charitable support. The noun 'fondation' designates an organization or charity.
Mon Dieu, c'est une trahison totale!
'My God, this is total betrayal!' Camille realizes that her father betrayed both her and ASK. The feminine noun 'trahison' denotes treachery or disloyalty.
Il a menti à tout le monde.
'He lied to everyone.' Camille sees clearly that Mathias manipulated everyone around him. The compound past tense 'a menti' comes from 'mentir'.
Camille? Tu as trouvé ce formulaire?
'Camille? Did you find that form?' Mathias returns from the kitchen holding two glasses. The past question 'tu as trouve' asks if someone found something.
Voici deux verres pour fêter ça!
'Here are two glasses to celebrate this!' Mathias approaches warmly to toast their reunion. The preposition 'voici' presents or introduces objects.
Oui, tout va très bien, papa.

'Yes, everything is fine, dad.' Camille conceals her devastation behind a composed expression. The polite reassurance 'tout va bien' claims that all is well. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

C'est un brouillon d'e-mail ouvert.
J'ai fait des promesses à Ulrika...
Pour qu'elle signe le contrat...
Mais je compte la décourager progressivement...
On peut la remplacer plus tard...
Utiliser la note de frais...
Pour une fondation animale...
Mon Dieu, c'est une trahison totale!
Il a menti à tout le monde.
Camille? Tu as trouvé ce formulaire?
Voici deux verres pour fêter ça!
Oui, tout va très bien, papa.

Horrified by the evidence of her father's treachery, Camille quickly hides her discovery as Mathias returns. The revelation leaves her questioning everything about her relationship with him. Now let's listen to the scene one last time.
À notre nouvelle vie!
